label: Dry Wood
reason: Dry wood is broader than cedar; offer timber, root and ambery directions.

choices.label: Cedary
choices.reference_note: Givaudan Cedarwood Virginia Oil USA illustrates wood that develops from mild and balsamic to drier wood. Pencil shavings are a recognition prompt.

choices.label: Rooty wood
choices.reference_note: IFF Vetiver Heart is a dry woody vetiver fraction with nutty and grapefruit nuances; it also supports the separate rooty-earth route.

choices.label: Dry ambery wood
choices.reference_note: IFF describes warm wood, dry amber and cedar facets. This is a woody-amber reference, not a sweet vanilla-resin amber accord.

label: Creamy Wood
reason: A sandalwood-like lane is already useful; milky and buttery variants would add near-synonyms at this print scale.

choices.label: Sandalwood-like
choices.reference_note: Givaudan describes creamy sandalwood with rosy nuances. It illustrates the creamy woody character; milky and buttery are comparisons.

label: Sheer Wood
reason: Keep one transparent woody-amber lane rather than inventing divisions based on strength or longevity.

choices.label: Soft woody amber
choices.reference_note: IFF describes smooth wood and amber with a velvety effect. This supports the soft woody-amber comparison, not a claim of low intensity.

label: Smoky
reason: A charred/tarry direction and a softer woody smoke direction help distinguish smoke qualities.

choices.label: Charred / tarry
choices.reference_note: Guaiacol is an identifiable fragrance chemical with a smoky phenolic character supported by sensory research. It illustrates smoke, not the whole tarry campfire impression.

choices.label: Smoked wood
choices.reference_note: Kanha Nature Oils describes smoky and rose-like facets and use in woody fragrances. It illustrates one woody-smoky direction; smoked tea is a separate recognition comparison.

label: Mossy / Forest
reason: Forest combines moss and leafy humus; those give two useful recognitions without adding an unrelated pine branch.

choices.label: Mossy
choices.reference_note: IFF Moss-Oak Absolute IFRA 43 is a named mossy reference with earthy, leathery and other facets. It is extracted from lichen, not a literal sample of damp forest moss.

choices.label: Leafy earth
choices.reference_note: IFF Patchouli Oil Indonesia For Life has woody-earthy, camphoraceous and mossy facets. It illustrates the earthy side of the leaf-litter comparison.

label: Petrichor
reason: Keep the focused rain-on-earth impression; beetroot is a comparison for its earthy facet, not a separate type of weather.

choices.label: Rain on earth
choices.reference_note: Geosmin supplies an earthy/musty facet associated with soil and beetroot, not the whole smell of rainfall. The linked analytical products document identity and odour; they are not recommended smelling samples.

label: Earthy / Rooty
reason: Separate humid patchouli-like earth from drier woody roots; both are accessible descriptive directions.

choices.label: Patchouli-like
choices.reference_note: IFF Patchouli Oil Indonesia For Life supports the woody-earthy direction, with camphoraceous and mossy facets; damp earth is a resemblance.

choices.label: Vetiver-like
choices.reference_note: IFF Vetiver Heart illustrates dry woody vetiver with nutty and grapefruit nuances. Roots are the extracted plant part; the same material supports a Wood route.

label: Mineral / Saline
reason: Wet-stone and sea-air associations offer different recognition prompts. Their references illustrate mineral and saline facets within broader woody profiles.

choices.label: Stony
choices.reference_note: Givaudan Vetiver Oil Haiti SIGNature has documented mineral facets within a woody-earthy profile. This illustrates a mineral association, not an exact smell of wet pebbles or a stone extract.

choices.label: Saline
choices.reference_note: Symrise identifies this de Laire base and its salty, mineral, woody-ambergris character. It is a specified manufacturer base, not salt itself or a reconstruction of skin and sea air.
choices.print_text: Sea air, skin after a sea swim

label: Hard Leather
reason: Split familiar leather surface from smoked hide; avoids asserting every leather smell is tar.

choices.label: Dry leather
choices.reference_note: Givaudan Safraleine illustrates a warm leathery facet alongside saffron-like spice and tobacco. It does not reproduce a complete leather belt or saddlery smell.

choices.label: Smoky hide
choices.reference_note: Firmenich Leather MD 936358 is a named material with smoky, leathery and burnt notes. It illustrates smoky leather without implying animal hide is present.

label: Suede
reason: Soft brushed leather is a useful single lane; subdividing soft and powdery leather is low-value in this selective print.

choices.label: Soft leather
choices.reference_note: The published Suede Petals demonstration formula on PDF page 2, the version with Safraleine, is a specific floral-leather composition for comparison. It is not a universal suede standard; the complete source formula identifies the blend.

label: Dry Leaf / Hay
reason: Unlit tobacco leaf and hay are useful distinct directions; retain the original realm-scoped tobacco membership.

choices.label: Dry tobacco leaf
choices.reference_note: Symrise Tabanon supplies a blond-tobacco facet with aromatic, spicy and balsamic aspects. It is a synthetic reference, not a cigar wrapper extract or a cigarette-smoke accord.

choices.label: Hay-like
choices.reference_note: Firmenich Hay Pays Abs is a named hay absolute with a soft herbal, woody and sweet balsamic character. It illustrates dried hay, with tobacco and moss nuances.

label: Animalic
reason: Soft warm musk and stronger animal-like character are meaningfully different recognitions.

choices.label: Warm skin / fur
choices.reference_note: Firmenich Muscone 962195 illustrates a soft sweet musk with warm animalic character. Skin and fur are comparisons, not the material source.

choices.label: Barnyard-like
choices.reference_note: Indole is an identifiable pungent animalic-floral material. It illustrates the stronger animalic facet only; stable hay, earth and the complete barnyard smell require other components.
